reasons: Both answers correctly identify oversell from async replicated decrements, note that strong consistency brings the latency back, propose per-region quotas, a reserve-then-pay flow and SKIP LOCKED, and cover failure modes. B states more clearly that the core problem is contention and fast rejection rather than raw throughput, and expects SKIP LOCKED on the existing RDS to handle these numbers, which fits rubric item 3 more closely. B also proposes a lower-risk phased path: keep a single owner and optimize the edge first, then move to escrow only if the remaining latency is shown to hurt. A goes straight to regional quotas.
